answer: The tide holds work receipts rather than names, so the mirror of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, capped per identity per epoch. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The plume of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
